title: Democratic senator Fetterman praises McCormick in video at GOP convention, September 9, 2026
dek: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., appeared in a video at the Republican Party's midterm convention on September 9, 2026, praising Republican Sen. Dave McCormick and pledging to work with President Trump on steel industry policy. The appearance comes amid reports of a close relationship between the two senators and internal Democratic criticism of Fetterman's bipartisan positioning.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Fetterman said in the video: 'Dave McCormick is the kind of senator that gets the job done, and he's going to fight for Pennsylvania. I'm proud to count him as my friend,' and added he would 'work together' with McCormick and Trump 'to fight and defend the steel way of life' in Pennsylvania.
bottom_line: Democratic senator endorses Republican colleague across the aisle at RNC convention, an unusual show of bipartisanship with broad major-outlet corroboration across political spectrum.
body:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., appeared on video at the Republican midterm convention on Wednesday night, September 9, praising Republican Sen. Dave McCormick and pledging collaboration with President Trump on steel industry policy.
"Yes, I'm a Democrat. Why am I here talking to you today? Because, well, I'm a common-sense Democrat," Fetterman said in the video, per NBC News. He continued: "I'm always going to stand with America. I'm always going to reject the extremes and socialism and the anti-American way of life. Dave McCormick is the kind of senator that gets the job done, and he's going to fight for Pennsylvania. I'm proud to count him as my friend." Fetterman pointed to a U.S. Steel mill and said: "That's exactly the kind of thing that we'll work together, and we'll work with President Trump, to fight and defend the steel way of life, right here in the Steel Valley," according to NBC News.
McCormick thanked Fetterman for his "friendship" and his "courage." Reaction in the convention hall was initially muted for Fetterman's message, with only a few attendees cheering, though the crowd applauded loudly when Fetterman concluded his remarks to introduce McCormick on stage, per NBC News.
Fetterman and McCormick have built a close bipartisan relationship and have launched a joint fundraising committee together. That committee triggered a wave of Democratic criticism of Fetterman, who has toyed with leaving the party but has vowed not to, according to NBC News.
The appearance followed reporting in The Wall Street Journal in which former aides to the senator provided texts and internal documents detailing Fetterman's lack of interest in engaging with constituents. After that story published, McCormick wrote on X: "These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman. They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him."
The Bottom Line: Fetterman's video appearance at the GOP convention, eight weeks before the midterm elections, exposes a fracture within Pennsylvania's Democratic leadership and raises questions about whether his relationship with McCormick signals a longer-term realignment or reflects isolated frustration with his party.
